increments.title: Increment branches stay local; the issue branch carries the run state to the remote
increments.goal: The loop works every increment on a branch that never leaves the checkout, lands accepted work on the issue branch and pushes that branch after each landed increment, asks nobody for a remote branch deletion, and still resumes a dead run from the state on the remote.
criteria: No agent working an increment pushes its increment branch: every step of an increment commits locally and pushes nothing.
The planner pushes the issue branch to the remote after each increment it lands, so the remote holds every accepted increment up to that point.

No agent page and no workflow prompt asks for a remote branch deletion: the `git push origin --delete` instruction is gone from workflows/agile-loop.js and from agents/planner.md, and no other page asks for one.
The run state a resume reads reaches the remote with the issue branch, and the resume path no longer depends on an increment branch existing on the remote.
A resumed run works the increments still open and does not redo an increment the run state records as closed.
The reviewer still receives the increment's diff range and can read that diff with the increment branch present only locally.
An increment the review does not accept stays unmerged as it does today, its commits stay local and reach no remote, and the note the planner closes with still names its branch.
The run opens one pull request, for the issue branch, as it does today.

return.plan:
GOAL: increment branches never leave the checkout; the issue branch carries every accepted increment and the run state to the remote; nobody is asked to delete a remote branch.

BLOCKER CHECK THE ISSUE DEMANDS (settled: not a blocker). The agents of an increment share one git directory, so a local branch is visible to all of them and nothing has to be pushed for them to see each other's commits. Evidence: (a) workflows/agile-loop.js is a workflow script that the runtime hands only `args`, `agent`, `log` and `phase` (its header comment, lines 30-56) — it has no filesystem, and every role reaches the work through `agent()`, i.e. a subagent of the one session, in that session's checkout; (b) no prompt anywhere in the script orders a `git pull`, and the only `git fetch` calls are the three at lines 719, 846 and 1354 — yet every role reads `<issueDir>/backlog.json` out of the working tree with the helper right after the previous step committed it, which is only sound in a shared checkout; (c) branchBlock's continue text tells the next agent to `check it out`, an operation on the session's own tree; (d) the reviewer judges `git diff <issueBranch>...HEAD`, i.e. the HEAD of that same tree. So the pushes are not load-bearing and the issue is built, not raised.

NOTE ON THE CODEMAP: the run state carries none (`codemap` printed nothing, and the index says `hasCodemap: false`), so the map in `moduleMap` is mine. The planner's third decompose ruling was right that agents/reviewer.md and README.md need no change — reviewer.md says nothing about pushing or fetching, and the README's PUB node is the issue branch already. Two files it left out do need changing: skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md (the shared brief orders every agent to push every step's commit, which contradicts criterion 1) and test-repo.sh (the suite that asserts the current push behaviour).

THE CHANGE, FILE BY FILE.

1) workflows/agile-loop.js — `branchBlock` (lines 833-849). Create form: keep the two things that put the resume point on the remote — recording the branch name with the helper's `branch` subcommand while still on the issue branch, and committing and pushing THAT change on the issue branch — and keep `git checkout -b <incrementBranch>`. Drop `push it with \`-u\``. Add, once and here only, the prohibition that the rest of the increment inherits: the increment branch stays in this checkout and is never pushed. Write it as a priced prohibition that quotes the rationalisation it counters (.claude/rules/authoring.md, failure class 'a rule skipped under pressure'), because the shared brief's own price ('an unpushed commit dies with the container') is exactly the excuse an agent will reach for: name the price — this environment's proxy refuses `git push origin --delete`, so a pushed increment branch can never be removed, and the increment's commits are disposable until the planner lands them. Continue form: replace `git fetch origin <incrementBranch>` and the 'if the remote does not have it, create it from <issueBranch> and push it with -u' fallback with a purely local instruction — check the branch out in this checkout, and create it from the issue branch if the checkout does not have it. No remote is named in either form except the issue branch's push.

2) workflows/agile-loop.js — `recordStep` (lines ~587-604). The line 'Commit it with your work and push the commit.' is emitted into every step's prompt, increment steps included, so it has to vary. Give the function a fourth parameter for whether this step pushes, defaulting to the pushing form, and emit the push clause only for it; the other form stops at the commit and says nothing more about pushing, because branchBlock already carries the prohibition and the brief says state each thing once. Call sites: pass the non-pushing form from the four increment dispatches (research ~1127, tests ~1168, implement ~1192, review ~1284) exactly when `incrementBranch` is non-empty, and the pushing form everywhere else. The predicate is `incrementBranch !== ''`, not `issueBranch !== ''`: when the run has no branch machinery at all (`issueBranch === ''`, the state loader named no branch) the increments are worked on the checkout's own branch and every step must go on pushing, or the run state never reaches a remote at all. `decompose` and `replan:<id>` always take the pushing form — the planner works the issue branch.

3) workflows/agile-loop.js — the state loader prompt (lines 700-733). Delete the whole trailing-copy paragraph, lines 717-724 ('The checkout's copy of the state can trail ... keep the checkout's copy.'): it exists only because an in-flight increment's state used to reach the remote on the increment branch, and after this change no increment branch is ever on a remote. Put one sentence in its place saying the run state reaches the remote only with the issue branch, so the checkout's copy is the whole of it and no fetch is needed. The closing line that forbids anything beyond the read-only git commands named in the prompt then leaves exactly one: `git branch --show-current`.

4) workflows/agile-loop.js — the replan prompt (lines 1351-1362). Accepted form: drop `git fetch origin <incrementBranch>` (the branch is local) and delete the whole delete sentence at 1356-1358, including its 'A failed delete is a line in your summary' softener. Keep 'check out <issueBranch>, merge <incrementBranch>, push <issueBranch>', and state why the push matters — the remote then holds every accepted increment and the run state a resume reads. The second push (of the close itself) already comes from recordStep's pushing form; do not state it twice. Not-accepted form: keep it as it is — do not merge, check out the issue branch first, name the unmerged branch in the note — and add that the branch's commits stay in this checkout and that it is not pushed.

5) workflows/agile-loop.js — comments that would go stale. Line 815-818 ('so the abandoned branch keeps its name on the remote') — the abandoned name lives in the state and the checkout now. Lines 827-832 (branchBlock's header) — say that the first dispatch pushes the issue branch, not the increment branch, and why. Lines 737-741 — add that increment branches never leave the checkout. Line 1470-1471 ('Every agent above commits and pushes its own step') — only the steps on the issue branch push.

6) workflows/agile-loop.js — the publish prompt (1478-1528) is unchanged. It already pushes `<issueBranch>` and opens one pull request; criterion 8 is 'as it does today'.

7) agents/planner.md, lines 108-113. Accepted bullet: keep 'merge the branch into the issue branch and push', give the push its reason (the remote then holds every increment landed so far, which is what a resumed run reads), and delete the clause 'once your close is committed and pushed, delete that merged branch from the remote — one issue, one pull request'. Not-accepted bullet: 'the branch stays on the remote' is now false — it stays in the checkout, unmerged and unpushed, and the note still names it.

8) skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md, the 'Commit your step, then push it' rule (lines 18-28). Today it is an unconditional 'push that commit straight away' plus 'Never keep a commit local while you carry on working', which flatly contradicts the increment prompts. Re-cut it on an observable predicate, per .claude/rules/authoring.md ('behaviour that depends on a condition' — a rule keyed to an observable predicate, both branches stated, never an exemption bolted onto the general rule). The predicate is what the prompt names: where the prompt asks for a push, push straight away, with the existing price and the existing quoted excuses; where the prompt names a branch that stays in the checkout, commit to it and push nothing, with its own price and its own quoted excuse (the pull to push 'just in case' is the one to quote). Constraints on the edit: keep the exact strings the repository suite already greps for — 'push the commit' anywhere in the page, the quoted excuse '"one push at the end will do"', the sentence fragment 'an unpushed commit dies with the container', 'Never push to the default branch' and its quoted excuse '"the work is done and the branch is green"' (test-repo.sh lines ~413, ~3125-3148). Two other places in the same page state the push and need the same predicate, once each and no more: the branch sentence at line 54 ('every commit and push of your step belongs to that branch') and the closing 'Record your step, commit it with your work, and push the commit.' at line 202. The record recipe's command chain at line 188 ends in `&& git push`; the template is what an agent copies, so it needs the predicate visible at it — one short clause is enough, and the implementer decides whether it rides in the chain or in the sentence under it.

9) test-repo.sh — see the test plan. Two of its existing cases assert the behaviour this increment removes and must be re-cut rather than left to fail.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. (a) Branches already on the remote from earlier runs are not cleaned up (the issue's non-goal). (b) Increment branches are still cut (non-goal). (c) A container that dies mid-increment loses that increment's local commits and the steps recorded on the increment branch; the run resumes from the last landed increment and works the open one again from the start, on a fresh `-take<n>` branch, because `incrementHasHistory` is false when no step of it is in the state the remote holds. That is exactly what criterion 4 asks for and no code change is needed for it. (d) One pre-existing hazard is left alone and is worth a follow-up issue: if a container dies mid-increment and the SAME checkout is resumed while still on the increment branch, the state loader returns that branch from `git branch --show-current` and the run treats it as the issue branch (which is why the publish prompt at line 1483 already apologises for it). It is out of this increment's criteria and unchanged in kind by this change.
moduleMap: workflows/agile-loop.js — the whole loop: every dispatch prompt and all the steering between them; one file, no imports — entry points for this change: the state loader prompt (lines 700-733, trailing-copy paragraph at 717-724), `recordStep` (587-604), `branchBlock` (833-849) and `nextBranchName` (819-825), the four increment dispatches that call them (research ~1127, tests ~1168, implement ~1192, review ~1284), the replan prompt (1345-1375), the publish prompt (1478-1528, unchanged)

agents/planner.md — the planner's role page: the cut, the codemap, how deep the chain goes, and what it does with the branch it is handed — entry point: the 'Every later call' bullets, lines 104-115 (the accepted/not-accepted/conflict branches; the remote-delete instruction is line 110)

skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md — the shared brief every agent preloads; the only channel that reaches an agent in a project that installed the plugin — entry points: 'Commit your step, then push it' (18-28), the branch sentence in 'Your brief' (line 54), the record recipe and its command chain (177-190), the closing 'Record your step, commit it with your work, and push the commit.' (line 202)

`bash test-repo.sh` — the only suite that owns any of the files this increment changes. Zero dependencies beyond `bash` and `node` on PATH (it shells out to `node` for its embedded driver); no install step, no build step.
There is no linter and no formatter in this repository.

return.testPlan:
WHETHER: tests are needed. Every criterion here is a fact about text the run emits — a prompt the workflow builds, a rule on a page — and test-repo.sh already asserts facts of exactly that kind, mechanically, with breaks named per case.

WHERE EVERYTHING GOES: one file, /home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh. Two shapes live in it and both are used below. (1) Bash cases: `if grep ...; then ok "..."; else no "..."; fi`, grouped under an `echo "=== <heading>"` line, each carrying a `# Break: ...` comment above it — that comment is this suite's convention (see lines ~1963, ~2333) and every case added or changed below carries one. (2) The embedded Node driver: the heredoc opened at line 737 with `cat >"$driver_tmp/driver.js" <<'JS'` writes a script that loads workflows/agile-loop.js as an AsyncFunction with a stub `agent`, collects every dispatch as `{label, agentType, prompt, schema}`, and asserts per mode. A mode needs three things: a fixture case in `contextFor` (line 1076), a branch in `main`'s if/else chain over `mode`, and a `run_driver "$wf" <mode> "<description>"` line in the loop at 2043. Existing fixtures name the issue branch `issue-branch` and the increment branch `issue-branch--i1`; `noState` (line 893) is the fresh-run fixture and `resumeState()` (line 907) the resumed one. Assertions that must hold in every mode go in the loops at the top of `main` (1240-1270). Prefer extending an existing mode over adding one wherever the fixture it already has is the fixture the case needs.

SUITE DOC: there is no CLAUDE.md beside test-repo.sh, and none is to be written. A CLAUDE.md at the repository root would load as project memory and be inherited by every subagent, which .claude/rules/agents.md forbids by design (it is why the rulebook is named rulebook.md), and a `.claude/rules/` page is scope this increment was not given. The conventions above are the whole of what the suite expects.

THREE EXISTING CASES MEET THIS CHANGE. Re-cut them, do not delete them and do not leave them failing.
  - test-repo.sh ~1406-1408, mode w8: `assertTrue(/\bpush\b/i.test(c.prompt), c.label + " is not told to push its step's commit")` over every step. It becomes: the steps on the issue branch (`decompose`, `replan:i1`) are told to push the commit; the increment's own steps are not. Its `run_driver` description at line 2052 names 'push the commit' and has to say what the case now checks.
  - test-repo.sh ~413, `grep -q 'push the commit' skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md`: stays green as long as the brief keeps that phrase, which the plan requires. Leave it alone; if the brief's wording drops the phrase, the case is wrong, not the brief.
  - test-repo.sh ~3125-3136, the brief's push rule as a priced prohibition quoting '"one push at the end will do"' and 'an unpushed commit dies with the container': stays green under the plan's constraint, and case 1.4 below is its counterpart for the new branch of the rule.

WHAT, CASE BY CASE. Every case is unit level, in /home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh, in the framework named above, and the command that runs it is `bash test-repo.sh` (the suite has no per-case runner).

Criterion 1 (no agent working an increment pushes its increment branch):
  1.1 — driver, fresh-run fixture with an issue branch (`noState`, e.g. mode w1): for every call whose label starts with `research:`, `tests:`, `implement:` or `review:`, no line of its prompt contains both a push instruction and the increment branch name `issue-branch--i1` → no such line in any of them. Match line by line, not over the whole prompt: the first dispatch legitimately pushes `issue-branch`, so a whole-prompt `/push/` assertion would be wrong. Break: put `push it with \`-u\`` back into branchBlock's create text.
  1.2 — driver, same fixture: the record instruction in each increment step's prompt does not carry the 'push the commit' clause, while `decompose`'s and `replan:i1`'s do → increment steps commit only. Break: make recordStep emit the push clause unconditionally.
  1.3 — driver, edge case, a fixture whose state names no branch (`branch: ''`, the shape already at line 882): every dispatched step's prompt still carries 'push the commit', because with no increment branch the work is on the checkout's own branch and the run state reaches the remote only through those pushes → all steps push. Break: make recordStep drop the push clause unconditionally, or key it on `issueBranch` instead of on `incrementBranch`.
  1.4 — bash grep over skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md: the push rule states both branches of its predicate — a push branch, and a branch for a prompt that names a branch staying in the checkout, that one carrying its own price and its own quoted excuse → both present. Break: delete the local branch from the brief, leaving the unconditional 'push that commit straight away'.

Criterion 2 (the planner pushes the issue branch after each increment it lands):
  2.1 — driver, fresh-run fixture, review accepted: the `replan:i1` prompt tells the planner to check out `issue-branch`, merge `issue-branch--i1` and push `issue-branch`, and its record instruction carries 'push the commit' → all three present. Break: delete the 'and push `<issueBranch>`' clause from the accepted branch of the replan prompt.

Criterion 3 (nobody asks for a remote branch deletion):
  3.1 — bash grep over the tracked files that are pages and code, excluding docs/issues (that directory is the record of past runs and quotes the old prompt verbatim — the licence case at line ~48 excludes it the same way): no file contains `git push origin --delete`, `git push origin :`, or prose asking for a merged branch to be deleted from the remote → no hits. Break: restore the delete instruction to agents/planner.md line 110.
  3.2 — driver, in the every-mode loop at the top of `main`: no dispatched prompt in any mode contains `--delete` → none. Break: restore the delete sentence to the replan prompt in workflows/agile-loop.js.

Criterion 4 (the resume path no longer depends on an increment branch on the remote):
  4.1 — driver, fresh-run fixture: the `load-state` prompt contains no `git show origin/`, no `merge-base --is-ancestor` and no `git fetch` → none of the three. Break: restore the trailing-copy paragraph (lines 717-724) to the state loader prompt.
  4.2 — driver, resumed fixture mid-increment (`resumeState()`, mode w2): the resumed dispatch (`implement:i1.0`) names `issue-branch--i1`, tells the agent to check it out in this checkout, and contains no `git fetch origin issue-branch--i1` → present, present, absent. Break: restore `git fetch origin ${incrementBranch}` to branchBlock's continue text.
  4.3 — driver, fresh-run fixture: the first dispatch of the increment still records the branch name with the helper's `branch` subcommand and still commits and pushes `issue-branch` before creating the increment branch — that push is what puts the resume point on the remote → both clauses present. Break: delete 'commit that state change and push `<issueBranch>`' from branchBlock's create text.

Criterion 5 (a resumed run works the open increments and does not redo a closed one): covered by cases the suite already has, which must keep passing unchanged after the state loader edit — mode w2 (a resumed run skips the recorded researcher and test-author and starts at the implementer, labels asserted at line ~1477), mode w3 (an all-closed backlog dispatches only `load-state` and `publish`, line ~1337) and mode w15 (a run resumed behind a closed increment counts it). Break: make `step()` dispatch a label the state records as done, or stop seeding `recorded` from the loaded index. Add nothing new here.

Criterion 6 (the reviewer still gets the diff range and can read it with the branch only local):
  6.1 — driver, fresh-run fixture: the `review:i1.0` prompt still contains `git diff issue-branch...HEAD` (the existing assertion at line ~1382 covers the range itself) and contains no `git fetch origin issue-branch--i1` → present, absent. Break: restore the fetch to branchBlock's continue text, which the review dispatch renders.

Criterion 7 (an unaccepted increment stays unmerged, local, and named in the note):
  7.1 — driver, mode w17 (the blocked-increment fixture): the closing prompt says not to merge, names `issue-branch--i1` for the note (both already asserted at line ~1621), and no line of it orders a push of that branch → the first two present, the third absent. Break: add an instruction to push the unmerged branch to the not-accepted branch of the replan prompt.

Criterion 8 (one pull request, for the issue branch):
  8.1 — driver, fresh-run fixture: the `publish` prompt orders `git push -u origin issue-branch` and no line of it orders a push of `issue-branch--i1` → present, absent. Break: change the publish prompt to push `"$(git branch --show-current)"` even when the run knows the issue branch.

NOTHING IS LEFT UNTESTED: every criterion above has at least one case that fails when the behaviour is broken or removed.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE: `bash test-repo.sh`, from the repository root, exit 0. That is the whole list.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED: nothing was run. No decision in this plan turns on a fact only a run can settle — every case above is an assertion over text I read in full — so the list is unrun and the first run belongs to whoever runs it downstream.
breaks: No agent working an increment pushes its increment branch: every step of an increment commits locally and pushes nothing. — put `push it with `-u`` back into branchBlock's create text in workflows/agile-loop.js (case 1.1), or make recordStep emit the 'push the commit' clause unconditionally (case 1.2), or delete the local branch from the shared brief's push rule (case 1.4)

The planner pushes the issue branch to the remote after each increment it lands, so the remote holds every accepted increment up to that point. — delete the 'and push `<issueBranch>`' clause from the accepted branch of the replan prompt in workflows/agile-loop.js (case 2.1)

No agent page and no workflow prompt asks for a remote branch deletion: the `git push origin --delete` instruction is gone from workflows/agile-loop.js and from agents/planner.md, and no other page asks for one. — restore the delete instruction to agents/planner.md line 110 (case 3.1) or the delete sentence to the replan prompt (case 3.2)

The run state a resume reads reaches the remote with the issue branch, and the resume path no longer depends on an increment branch existing on the remote. — restore the trailing-copy paragraph (git fetch / merge-base --is-ancestor / git show origin/<branch>) to the state loader prompt (case 4.1), restore `git fetch origin ${incrementBranch}` to branchBlock's continue text (case 4.2), or delete the 'commit that state change and push `<issueBranch>`' clause from branchBlock's create text (case 4.3)

A resumed run works the increments still open and does not redo an increment the run state records as closed. — make `step()` dispatch a label the loaded state records as done, or stop seeding `recorded` from the loaded index (existing modes w2, w3, w15)

The reviewer still receives the increment's diff range and can read that diff with the increment branch present only locally. — restore `git fetch origin ${incrementBranch}` to branchBlock's continue text, which the review dispatch renders, or drop `git diff <issueBranch>...HEAD` from the reviewer's prompt (case 6.1)

An increment the review does not accept stays unmerged as it does today, its commits stay local and reach no remote, and the note the planner closes with still names its branch. — add an instruction to push the unmerged branch to the not-accepted branch of the replan prompt (case 7.1)
The run opens one pull request, for the issue branch, as it does today. — change the publish prompt to push `"$(git branch --show-current)"` even when the run knows the issue branch (case 8.1)
rulings: Built the change instead of raising the blocker the issue names, because the agents of an increment share one git directory — the workflow script has no filesystem and reaches every role through `agent()` as a subagent of the one session, no prompt anywhere orders a `git pull` before reading the state the previous step committed, and the reviewer judges `git diff <issueBranch>...HEAD` in that same tree; wrong costs the whole increment, since unpushed increment branches would leave each agent unable to see the last one's commits.

Wrote no suite doc for test-repo.sh and told the test-author to write none, because a CLAUDE.md at the repository root would load as project memory inherited by every subagent, which .claude/rules/agents.md forbids by design, and a path-scoped `.claude/rules/` page is scope this increment was not given; wrong costs one small doc a later increment adds.

Left the pre-existing hazard where a container that dies mid-increment and resumes in the same checkout, still on the increment branch, makes the loop treat that branch as the issue branch, because no criterion of this increment covers it and this change does not alter its kind; wrong costs one run that pushes an increment branch and opens its pull request, which the human sees and can close.

Set the closed list of commands to `bash test-repo.sh` alone rather than `bash test.sh`, because that is the only one of the eight suites that owns any file this increment touches; wrong costs one regression in an untouched suite that the pull request's next run catches.
return.summary: The increment is buildable as specified: the agents of an increment share one checkout, so nothing has to be pushed for them to see each other's work, and the issue's blocker case does not apply. The change drops the increment-branch pushes and the state loader's remote trailing-copy read from workflows/agile-loop.js, deletes the remote-delete instruction there and in agents/planner.md, makes the planner's push of the issue branch the thing that carries every accepted increment and the run state to the remote, and re-cuts the shared brief's push rule on the predicate of what the prompt names — with test-repo.sh's driver cases, including the three that assert today's behaviour, re-cut to match.
